subject.title: [Feature Request] Unified Built-in Sandbox with Multi-Platform Support and Tiered Presets

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a staged core plugin-isolation architecture with secure-by-default sandbox presets, or keep core sandboxing focused on opt-in tool-execution backends?
rationale: The choice changes core trust boundaries, plugin SDK compatibility, default configuration, upgrade behavior, platform guarantees, and credential handling; code inspection cannot determine the intended product and security contract.

options.title: Stage core isolation milestones
options.body: Approve the direction but split design and implementation into separately reviewed default-policy, IPC, manifest, credential, platform, and migration milestones.

options.title: Narrow to tool sandboxing
options.body: Limit core work to improving the existing tool and browser sandbox backends, leaving native plugin process isolation outside the current roadmap.

options.title: Defer default changes
options.body: Continue adding opt-in isolation backends while postponing secure-by-default presets and plugin SDK boundary changes until compatibility requirements are clearer.

recommendation.title: Stage core isolation milestones
recommendation.body: Approve the direction but split design and implementation into separately reviewed default-policy, IPC, manifest, credential, platform, and migration milestones.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the clearest existing architecture-level direction in this issue and are connected to the affected sandbox and plugin-loader history.
